proposal:
SCOPE: one sound extension rule (RX), one work monovariant, audit findings, one pinned-v5 fixture. Nothing was executed. No all-CNF bound is claimed, and every lemma below needs independent proof.

AUDIT (read from the supplied code).
(a) compression._verify_certificate rebuilds blocks from every dense original clause, requires each used form to lie inside the block mask, compares local truth tables and checks all r^2 entries of P*L=I. Every skip returns the input unchanged. I find no omitted-block defect.
(b) Cost finding in test_elim.attempt: all |pos|*|neg| resolvents are materialised, and canon's pairwise subsumption runs before the admissibility test. This repeats for each candidate variable until one is accepted, at every node. The worst case is Theta(m^4) subset tests per attempt (about 7e10 at m=512), although an accepted state never exceeds m clauses. It is polynomial but independent of peak.
(c) refute rescans the whole formula for every tuple, up to max_tuples*m*w*n literal visits per node. I conjecture that this, not peak, is the pigeonhole h=4 cost.

RULE RX (rectangle extension). This is Bounded Variable Addition (Manthey-Heule-Biere 2012; SBVA, Haberlandt-Green-Heule 2023), cited from memory; it is not new mathematics. Take a literal set L and a clause set Gamma with |L|,|Gamma|>=2, where no clause of Gamma mentions a variable of L and l v C is in F for every pair. With x fresh, set F' = F minus {l v C} plus {l v x : l in L} plus {-x v C : C in Gamma}. Fire only if the literal count strictly drops: (|L|-1)(|Gamma|+sum|C|) > 2|L|.
Lemma (two lines, needs Lean): the projection of Models(F') away from x equals Models(F). One inclusion is resolution on x. For the other, set x:=1 iff some l in L is false. So RX is exact for both SAT and UNSAT, with no hypothesis on clauses outside the rectangle. Arbitrary extras cannot make it unsound, and added clauses cannot remove a rectangle. SMF-2 (my 00065) is a quotient and needs every clause touching the pair to conform; RX does not.

WORK INVARIANT. Let lambda be the total number of literal occurrences. Each RX step strictly decreases lambda, does not increase the clause count, and adds one variable. So there are at most lambda0 steps and at most n+lambda0 variables.
- Detection: key every clause minus one literal (sum|C|^2 literal operations), group keys R into literal sets L_R, count literal pairs, and grow L by intersection. A crude bound is O(lambda*n*log lambda) bit operations per step and O(lambda^2*n*log lambda) in total.
- Certificate: the list of (x, L, Gamma). The checker tests freshness and set membership only, O(lambda) per step, with no 2^w tables and no width-8 cap.
- Placement: run once at the root, after BLQ and the core probe and before DP. Never re-run it, because clause-count-nonincreasing DP can undo marginal 2x2 steps and ping-pong.

NEON58. On the 16-variable quotient the only qualifying rectangles are {-a_i,-a_i'} x (selections on the remaining pairs). Taking the lowest pair first, each side goes 16 -> 10 -> 6 -> 4 clauses (lambda 64 -> 36 -> 24 -> 20). The fourth step is literal-neutral and does not fire. The result has 22 variables and 32 clauses and is the fixture, up to renaming; I do not know v5's actual quotient numbering.
Hand trace of pinned v5 on the fixture:
- Every exact-support block holds one clause, so compression skips with all_variables_in_odd_blocks.
- The core probe returns no_clauses_removed.
- Root elim accepts 21 eliminations in the order 1..16, 17, 20, 18, 21, 19 and ends on complementary units. The root IALH outcome cannot change the answer.
- Prediction: sat=false, peak=0 (secondary: accepted_dp=21).
Before RX, eliminating a_i needs 4x8 resolvents and is rejected. After RX it needs 4x1.

INDEPENDENT-TEST PREDICTIONS (unimplemented). For the k-pair family at k=5,6,7 (20/24/28 variables, 89/164/305 clauses), RX fires 2(k-1) times and leaves k^2+4k clauses, after which pinned v5 gives peak 0. Adding one clause that uses single pair members leaves the RX steps unchanged; I do not predict the peak in that case.

EXTENSION TO ARBITRARY CNF AND THE OBSTRUCTION. RX applies to any CNF at polynomial cost and is the identity when nothing fires. It does nothing for:
- parity or Tseitin blocks, where no two clauses differ in exactly one literal;
- the ordering principle;
- kernel-free families whose useful definitions are not rectangles of input clauses (Cook's pigeonhole extension variables);
- rectangles with deleted cells.
After RX the residual DP can still be STUCK, and search and IALH costs then return unbounded.
missing_theorem:
MT-A (routine, unchecked): a Lean proof of the RX projection lemma for arbitrary width, the lambda monovariant, and the stated bit bounds for detection and certificate checking.

MT-B (rectangle closure, conjecture): suppose F contains Dist(T_1),...,Dist(T_r), the full CNF distributions of read-once AND/OR trees over literals with pairwise disjoint leaves, and is otherwise arbitrary. Then every maximal RX sequence reaches literal count at most c*sum|T_s| + lambda(extras). BVA is known to be order-dependent on overlapping rectangles, so confluence is false in general. The disjoint-leaf hypothesis is the proposed repair and is unproved.

MT-C (residual, conjecture): for two-sided group-transversal systems (k groups per side of arbitrary sizes, a positive part made of unions of whole groups, one negative tree per side), RX followed by pinned elim never returns STUCK. It should use at most n+2k eliminations, each attempt with at most max(k,g)^2 resolvents. Any ordering used by the min-product rule must be covered.

Boundary: one tree per side cannot be relaxed to many trees with an arbitrary positive part. Disjoint clauses (-p v -q) plus an arbitrary positive CNF already encode general SAT. A statement that RX plus the v5 residual does p(N) total work on every CNF is equivalent in strength to P=NP and is not claimed.

Exact gap: a polynomial procedure that chooses extension variables which are not syntactic rectangles, with a bound on the subsequent DP and search work.
self_attack:
1. RX is a known preprocessing technique. The contribution is only checked integration, a truth-table-free certificate and total-work accounting.
2. It is syntactic. One missing rectangle cell blocks the step, and covering near-rectangles optimally is minimum biclique cover (NP-hard, hard to approximate). Greedy choice is order-dependent.
3. The fixture tests pinned v5 on a hand-reencoded instance. It does not test detection. My tie-break trace could be wrong; I believe other tie orders also end UNSAT, but that is unproved.
4. RX adds variables. That can enlarge the IALH window set and place fresh variables late in the search order, so peak or time may worsen on other inputs. Run before BLQ it destroys even-block structure, hence the fixed position after BLQ and the core probe.
5. Efficacy is not robust. Extra clauses that give a pair member many negative occurrences make DP reject its elimination, and search returns. Soundness is unaffected.
6. Pigeonhole h=5 total work is untouched. BVA compresses pairwise at-most-one constraints, but the refutation still needs counting. No claim is made.
7. The Theta(m^4) attempt cost and the per-node IALH rescans remain. Guarding attempts by |pos|*|neg| changes which eliminations are accepted and may change peaks, so it needs its own regression run.
8. The peak of 8 at k=4 is a single observation. No lower bound for v5 without RX is claimed.
mechanism_signature: RX-1: one-shot root rectangle extension (BVA-type; one-way definition forcing x true whenever a literal of L is false). Exact model projection. Literal-count monovariant with at most lambda0 steps. Set-membership certificate with no local truth tables and no width cap. Placed after BLQ and the core probe, before clause-count-nonincreasing DP. Sound under arbitrary extra clauses; efficacy only conjectured for disjoint read-once distributions.
delta_from_prior: SMF-2 (00065) was an exact quotient: it removed a variable pair and needed every clause touching the pair to match a gate pattern, so one extra clause broke it. In 00064 the one-way OR definitions had to be present in the input. RX synthesises the one-way definition as a fresh extension variable from a complete clause rectangle, and other clauses on the same variables are unconstrained. It needs no GF(2) structure, stabilizer or module. Its certificate is width-independent, unlike BLQ's 2^w local tables. New audit items are the Theta(m^4) pre-admissibility subsumption cost in attempt and the RX/DP ping-pong hazard. New negative boundary: the many-tree generalisation is NP-complete, so MT-C cannot be widened that way.
